messages:
incbot: INCIDENT alert — continuous-batcher latency spike detected for customer-facing pools. Auto-pager triggered. Root metric: kv_cache_evictions/sec x10, p95 latency from 180ms -> 2.4s. Priority: P1
Priya: paging in — I see a steep rise in KV cache churn correlated with continuous-batch microbatch sizes collapsing into tiny slices. Likely feedback where evictions cause more cache misses -> smaller batches -> queueing.
Samir: confirmed on graphs. In-flight queue depth up 4x on us-east-1 consumers. Many small microbatches observed.
Tess: any recent rollout of prefetch/kv heuristics? I don't see new commits in the last 30m. Could be config drift from autoscaling.
Marco: not a code deploy. Controller logs show repeated: "attempting to refill kv; microbatch size target=1" every 200ms.
Priya: full stack trace snippet from continuous-batcher controller logs:
```
2026-03-15T10:12:08Z controller INFO target_microbatch=1 observed_queue_ms=1200 kv_eviction_rate=978
2026-03-15T10:12:09Z cache WARN evict key=xxx reason=memory_pressure
2026-03-15T10:12:09Z batcher DEBUG flush microbatch_count=1
```
Samir: that shows a feedback loop. Eviction -> cache miss -> smaller batches -> more load -> more evictions. We need to break the loop.
Tess: early mitigation: disable prefetch on affected pools and raise min_microbatch to 8 to avoid collapse. Can do via feature flags.
Marco: prepping flag change. Which pools? prod-us-east-1 and prod-eu-west-1 are the ones with user-facing slot spikes.
Priya: set target: PREFETCH_ENABLED=false for pool=prod-us-east-1, MIN_MICROBATCH=8 for both clusters. Apply to prod-eu after verifying us-east.
ops-bot: Executing runbook step: toggle feature flags via ops-api. Endpoint: POST /flags/batch-config
Samir: doing US-EAST now. Patch payload:
```
{ "pool": "prod-us-east-1", "flags": { "prefetch_enabled": false, "min_microbatch": 8 } }
```
ops-bot: 200 OK — flags applied to prod-us-east-1 (rollout 100%).
Tess: monitoring telemetry — KV eviction rate dropping?
Priya: initial signal: evictions/sec down from ~980 -> ~220 in the last 90s, p95 latency trending down 2.4s -> 760ms. Still elevated but moving.
Marco: queuing pressure also falling. However microbatch variance still shows jitter — some clients still producing tiny batches. Recommend fast restart of continuous-batcher controller to reset internal admission state.
Samir: agree. I'm going to do a rolling restart of the controller deployment with zero-downtime flags. Command:
```
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/continuous-batcher-controller --context=prod-us-east-1
```
Priya: coordinate with oncall in eu before restarting eu. We might need to stagger to avoid global impact.
Tess: I'll hold on eu until us-east stabilizes.
ops-bot: Restart initiated for prod-us-east-1 controller. Pod1 terminating, Pod2 draining.
Marco: Post-restart metrics — controller started with fresh counters. Observed microbatch targets stabilizing around 8-12. p95 improved to 420ms. KV evictions continuing to drop.
Samir: great. Can we safely apply the same flag change to prod-eu-west-1 now?
Priya: yes, do it. Also while we're here, enable a conservative batching threshold to avoid rapid min_microbatch oscillation: set BATCH_JITTER_WINDOW_MS=300 and MAX_MICROBATCH=64.
Samir: applying EU patch now. Payload:
```
{ "pool": "prod-eu-west-1", "flags": { "prefetch_enabled": false, "min_microbatch": 8, "batch_jitter_window_ms": 300, "max_microbatch": 64 } }
```
ops-bot: 200 OK — flags applied to prod-eu-west-1.
Tess: EU metrics following flags — p95 from 1.9s -> 650ms within 2m. KV eviction rate down 5x.
Marco: still seeing a small subset of clients that hammer with tiny seq lengths causing local batching to underflow. We should consider a short-term token-based rate limiter on microbatch admission for noisy clients.
Priya: agree but that's a medium-term change. For immediate customer impact: which customers saw errors/timeouts? Any SLO breaches?
Samir: Edge logs show increased 502s for customer acct: storefront-inc between 10:08–10:20. Errors peaked at 12% of their requests. Our SLA window will need notification.
Tess: capture evidence: saved traces and request ids, set incident state: mitigated (flags+restart), monitoring. Assign: Samir to make customer impact note and notify CSM. Marco to file follow-up bug for admission-rate limiter. Priya to run postmortem once stabilized.
Samir: drafting message for CSM: short summary, impact window, mitigation steps, next steps for prevention.
Marco: created GH issue #4876 "microbatch admission jitter: admission backpressure and noisy-client isolation" and attached graphs.
ops-bot: Incident role update: state=mitigated, severity=P1->P2 pending postmortem.
Priya: timeline note for postmortem: root cause = KV cache feedback loop under very-high concurrency with microbatch collapse; immediate fix = disable prefetch + raise min_microbatch + restart controller; long-term = admission rate limiter + better eviction heuristics.
Tess: any objections to rolling back prefetch permanently? I think heuristics need work; prefer to re-enable with tuned params after tests.
Samir: +1. We'll keep prefetch disabled for 24h and run load tests.
Priya: ok. Closing pager for now — watch the dashboards for 1 hour, escalate if p95>800ms or kv_evictions/sec >300.
incbot: Pager cleared by Priya at 10:20Z.
Marco: quick note for ops runbook: add step to set MIN_MICROBATCH when kv_eviction_rate > 500 as an automated fallback. I'll submit PR to runbooks repo.
Samir: filing customer notification now. Will post link here when done.
Tess: thanks all — nice coordination.
Samir: customer notification sent to CSM: https://redwood.internal/notes/incident/3612300123
Priya: putting follow-up checklist in tickets and assigning owners. We'll reconvene for a 1hr blameless postmortem sync if metrics not back to normal by 11:15.
Marco: logging action items: [ ] Runbook PR, [ ] Admission limiter spec, [ ] Eviction heuristic tuning, [ ] Load test reproducer.
Priya: end of thread for oncall handoff.
